subject: physics
question_text: Does a body radiate heat at 0 K? Does it radiate heat at 0°C?

verification.note: Asked in TS Inter I-Year Physics Paper-I, March 2025 (Q7) — Section A, 2 marks. The 1 + 1 mark split, one mark for each of the two parts asked, is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced from that paper. Physics hand-checked: by Stefan’s law the emitted power goes as T⁴, so at T = 0 K it is exactly zero; 0 °C = 273 K, which is above absolute zero, so a body at 0 °C does radiate.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: At 0 K — no
lines: No. At 0 K the absolute temperature is
A body at absolute zero radiates nothing.
steps.margin_note: First mark. The answer no, with T = 0 put into Stefan’s law.
steps.why: Stefan’s law makes the emitted power proportional to the fourth power of the absolute temperature, so it becomes zero only when the absolute temperature itself is zero.
common_mistakes: Saying a body at 0 K still radiates a little. At T = 0 the emitted power is exactly zero.

recall.must_convey: That at 0 K the body does not radiate, because E = σT⁴ is zero.
accept: sigma T to the fourth is zero

steps.memory_tip: E = σT⁴. Put T = 0 and the emitted power is exactly zero.

steps.label: At 0 °C — yes
lines: Every body above absolute zero radiates.
At 0 °C the absolute temperature is 273 K,
so the body does radiate, only weakly.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The answer yes, with the conversion 0 °C = 273 K.
steps.why: Absolute zero is at −273 °C, so 0 °C is 273 degrees above it. Radiation stops only at the zero of the kelvin scale, not at the zero of the Celsius scale.
common_mistakes: Reading 0 °C as no temperature at all. On the kelvin scale it is 273 K.

recall.must_convey: That at 0 °C the body does radiate, because 0 °C is 273 K.
reject: sigma T to the fourth is zero

steps.memory_tip: 0 °C is 273 K, not zero. Only 0 K stops the radiation.

insider_note: Two questions, one mark each. The conversion 0 °C = 273 K is the line that earns the second mark — a bare yes does not.
